transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-05-06
Time: 15:00 PT
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Marco (Redwood CSM), Aisha (CTO), Devon (ML Eng), Chris (Infra), Sara (Security)

Summary (auto): POC weekly sync - onboarding status, access, environment readiness and quick tuning notes.

[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh we can kick off. Quick roll call?
[00:06] Aisha: Yeah this is Aisha, CTO at MedData Labs.
[00:09] Devon: Devon here, ML.
[00:11] Chris: Chris, infra.
[00:12] Sara: Sara from security.
[00:14] Jordan: Great, Priya and Marco with me from Redwood. We wanted to run through the access checklist, the initial benchmark we ran last week, and next steps.
[00:25] Priya: I'll start with the environment readiness notes. We saw the VPC looks spun up, there was a question about whether the peering connection is two-way, I think Chris kicked off the peering request?
[00:33] Chris: Yeah we created a peering request yesterday, waiting on route table updates. Also need to confirm the outbound egress to Redwood's collector IP range, we've put a note in the ticket.
[00:45] Priya: Perfect. For the POC to run, we need a service account with IAM role that allows creating ephemeral containers / pods, and access to the KMS key for encryption of model artifacts if you're using private deployment. If you plan to use Redwood Hosted that's simpler but for dedicated/private we need the key.
[01:05] Sara: On KMS, we saw the KMS policy doc you shared but we need an example of the exact IAM role bindings. Can you send us the minimal perms?
[01:12] Jordan: Absolutely, I'll share the sample policy. We'll also attach the SOC2 snippet with the KMS integration example.
[01:18] Devon: Quick question, Priya — in last week's smoke test the latency numbers seemed to jump occasionally. Any immediate tuning we should try?
[01:26] Priya: Yeah so couple things: sequence length distribution in your requests was spikier than expected — a bunch of 5k token requests mixed with short ones which ruins batching heuristics. We recommended a predictor to cap prompt length or chunk. Also, try enabling prefix KV caching for repeated context, that reduced tokens by about 20% in our tests.
[01:48] Devon: Okay, makes sense. We can do chunking at the client side initially.
[01:52] Priya: Also we noticed you were using the q4_0 quant profile on the 80B model, which is good for cost but if you need latency consistency we can suggest smaller model variant or switch to dedicated infra with faster GPUs.
[02:05] Aisha: We're sensitive to cost but also need consistent latency for triage flows. What's the hybrid recommendation?
[02:11] Priya: Typically customers start hosted for dev, then move to dedicated for stable latency, and keep a hosted fallback for bursts. Redwood's routing can failover to a cheaper model if capacity drops. We'll put together a small decision matrix.
[02:26] Jordan: Also to call out — Redwood Console now provides token-level latency breakdowns which helps tie cost back to specific routes, I can show that in the next demo.
[02:36] Marco: Quick note, Devon, we uploaded a shared benchmark spreadsheet, link in the invite. It has the smoke numbers and the raw traces.
[02:45] Devon: Yep I saw that, thanks.
[02:48] Jordan: On network — Chris, once you confirm the service account and egress rules we can try the smoke benchmark from our side and from yours to compare.
[02:57] Chris: I'm aiming to have the service account JSON and the allowlist by Monday. One question — do you need a static IP for the peering tunnel?
[03:06] Priya: We don't require a static IP for the Redwood hosted collector, we provide a CIDR range to allowlist; for dedicated/private deployments we prefer peering or VPC endpoints and then you manage routing.
[03:18] Chris: Got it. We'll stick with peering for now.
[03:22] Sara: Security question — what logs do you capture and how long are they retained? We want to ensure PHI isn't stored long-term.
[03:30] Jordan: We capture request/response metadata for observability but can mask or drop payloads. For hosted we retain logs per the default retention (30 days) but we have enterprise packages for longer retention or customer-managed log sinks. We'll include the options in the doc.
[03:45] Sara: And is there a way to do customer-managed KMS so keys never leave our control?
[03:49] Priya: Yes, we support customer-managed KMS for private and dedicated, and for hosted you can integrate via a key-wrapping flow. We'll get the integration diagram in the security pack.
[03:58] Aisha: Great. On timeline — we're expecting to run a more thorough benchmark next week and then decide on committed capacity by end of May.
[04:05] Jordan: Sounds good. We'll put together the committed capacity options and pricing tiers.
[04:09] Devon: About the benchmark — for the test plan, we want to run both throughput and tail-latency scenarios, and also evaluate quantization impact. Priya, can you outline the configs?
[04:19] Priya: Sure. Plan: run three profiles — hosted small instance with q4_0, dedicated with bf16 on A100s (or equivalent), and a mid-tier dedicated with mixed precision. We'll measure p50/p95/p99, tokens/sec and cost per 1k tokens. I'll also include KV cache on/off cases.
[04:34] Devon: Perfect. Also we have some sensitive prompts — we can anonymize but we'll need to ensure no PII/PHI is retained.
[04:41] Sara: Yes, confirm how prompt redaction works and please include the retention window.
[04:45] Priya: We'll add the redaction/obfuscation checklist.
[04:48] Jordan: We'll also share the security pack and the SOC2 excerpts after the call.
[04:53] Marco: FYI we had a question earlier about model rollouts — if you pin a model version and we detect a regression in evals, Redwood can auto-fallback. That's part of the rollout policies.
[05:03] Aisha: That's helpful. One more ops question — if we go dedicated, can we burst to hosted in spikes?
[05:09] Priya: Yes, burst capacity is supported. We recommend defining burst thresholds in the autoscaling policy. We'll provide recommended settings based on your expected QPS.
[05:21] Devon: Any blockers left from our side?
[05:23] Chris: Route tables and IAM role docs from Redwood. Once we have the sample IAM policy I can get infra to wire it up.
[05:29] Sara: And the SOC2 snippets and KMS example for security review.
[05:33] Jordan: We'll send those.
[05:35] Marco: I'll set up the follow-up demo to show Console transit details and token-level cost per route — aim for next Thursday?
[05:41] Aisha: Next Thursday works for us.
[05:43] Jordan: Cool. We'll schedule and send calendar.
[05:45] Priya: Quick note — one of the spikes we saw hinted at long-running KV cache misses, maybe due to slightly different prompt prefixes. If you can standardize prefixes that would help.
[05:57] Devon: We'll try to consolidate.
[06:00] Jordan: Ok, recap of next steps: Jordan share security pack + pricing, Priya run smoke benchmark and share configs, Chris provide IAM and peering details, Sara confirm KMS requirements. We'll reconvene next Thursday for the Console walkthrough.
[06:17] Aisha: Thanks everyone.
[06:18] Jordan: Thanks, bye.

Notes and artifacts referenced: shared benchmark spreadsheet (link in calendar invite), security pack (will be attached), sample IAM/KMS policy snippet (to be sent).

Transcription notes: occasional microphone overlap; some acronyms transcribed incorrectly (e.g., 'q4_0' shown as 'Q 40' in one of the automated lines).
